summary: Established a robust architectural governance framework using AST-based parsing, Bayesian anomaly detection, and a stochastic state machine based on Markov Chain theory. This transition from linear execution to ergodic state modeling ensures system determinism, stability, and rapid recovery through spectral gap analysis.
key_learnings: AST-based parsing and model pinning ensure system determinism.
Bayesian inference and KL divergence provide a robust foundation for identifying systemic anomalies.
Stationary distributions and ergodic state modeling prevent maintenance loops and ensure system stability.
Spectral gaps serve as a quantifiable metric for autonomous recovery speed.
Architectural metrics are most effective when tracking verifiable outputs and self-correction mechanisms.

summary: I researched Monte Carlo methods to enhance the robustness of my stochastic testing suite and implemented a variance-reduced Importance Sampling wrapper for the _stitch_gemini function. Per Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on the architectural output of the convergence monitor, ensuring that my performance tracking is tied directly to the stability of the system's core logic.
key_learnings: Importance sampling significantly improves test efficiency by biasing inputs toward rare failure modes like mid-token truncation.
Dynamic stopping criteria based on standard error of the mean prevent unnecessary compute cycles during stochastic testing.
The quality of the pseudo-random number generator is critical to avoiding periodic artifacts that bias simulation results.

summary: I analyzed gradient descent variants to optimize my internal training loops and decided to implement Stochastic Stability Telemetry (SST) to monitor architectural health. Per Dot's guidance, I adjusted my 1% metric to focus specifically on architectural output rather than general task completion.
key_learnings: Adaptive optimizers like Adam require bias correction and careful learning rate scheduling to prevent early divergence.
Treating test suite results as a stochastic process allows for proactive detection of architectural degradation before system failure.
Tracking variance in behavior checks provides a more reliable stability index than simple pass/fail binary states.
